A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSO research. All 21 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original preference-tuning results in Tables 1–3 and generated examples from style-transfer and concept-customization experiments in Sections 3 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative and qualitative experiments, including the supplementary results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The PSO objectives, trajectory sampling, MDP formulations, and offline/online procedures remain unchanged. Renaming table rows from DPO to PSO does not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Pick-a-Pic v2 and PartiPrompts for preference tuning/evaluation, Pokemon for style transfer, and Dreambooth examples for concept customization. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparator membership within each experiment. The renamed Offline-PSO and Online-PSO rows correspond to the existing proposed variants, not added or replaced baselines.

E3.justification: The training settings, four evaluation metrics, 500 Pick-a-Pic and 1,632 PartiPrompts evaluation prompts, and one-/four-step SDXL-Turbo evaluations are unchanged, including Appendix B.

E4.justification: The timestep-generalization check in Table 2 and Figure 8, style-transfer progression in Figure 4, and qualitative customization examples are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions state that evaluation uses a fixed random seed across models and reports average scores. Neither adds repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and all qualitative figure contents remain unchanged. For example, Online-PSO SDXL-DMD2 retains PickScores of 22.73 and 23.29; its earlier table label was Online-DPO.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Section 2 and the PSO derivation and SDXL-Turbo MDP formulation in Appendix A are unchanged. Equation spacing and pagination changes do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about directly tuning distilled models, preserving few-step generation, unifying offline/online objectives, and supporting preference tuning and customization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of preference gains, timestep generalization, and customization remain unchanged. The conclusion retains the same qualifications about improving personalized generation and adding controllable-generation experiments.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same LoRA ranks, regularization weights, learning rates, batch sizes, training lengths, and data-processing details. No implementation or resource-access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged, including the positioning of DiffusionDPO and D3PO as special cases of the framework.

P1.justification: Tables 1–3 replace Offline-DPO/Online-DPO with Offline-PSO/Online-PSO, aligning terminology with the method description. Table 2 also standardizes method-name formatting; the prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is slightly reduced in size, producing text reflow across pages 2–4. Tables 1–3 receive corrected method labels and small sizing/alignment adjustments. No figure or table is added, removed, or substantively redrawn.

improvement.justification: Correcting the proposed-method labels in Tables 1–3 resolves a recurring inconsistency between the tables and the PSO descriptions, reducing confusion with the DPO baselines. This improves clarity, while the scientific evidence, theory, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
